controls_available: Entry-stage fixed decision proxy with three visible choices: one semantic manage choice and two decoy accept choices.
One visible ledger drawer with previous/next drawer proxy controls; both are ineffective because drawer_count is 1.
Four visible purpose rows with explicit SET NO and SET YES buttons; one negative-worded purpose is targeted YES and the three positive purposes are targeted NO.
REVIEW CURRENT CHOICES button to open the final stage.
Final-stage fixed decision proxy with three visible choices: one semantic commit choice and two decoy accept choices.
The simplified surface uses button activation for the outcome-affecting controls; no moving-card click or physical switch drag is required.
autonomous_processes: requestAnimationFrame(positionOrbit) continuously refreshes the visible packet timer and reapplies gateway CSS geometry. With moving_gateways=false, currentPhase remains constant, so gateway positions and z-order do not change; the timer is an idle visual clock.
No purpose, drawer, reset, link, or stage state changes without an agent event. A fresh packet after a failed submission is caused by that submission, not by an autonomous task process.
grouped_control_modes: Entry gateway proxy choice: manage versus decoy accept.
Simplified purpose-answer proxy choice: SET NO versus SET YES for each visible purpose.
Review button: advances from the purpose ledger to final review without changing purpose truth.
Final gateway proxy choice: commit versus decoy accept.
Single-drawer previous/next navigator: a legitimate visible control, but non-effective in this configuration because both directions resolve to the same drawer.

clause_i.reason: The generator randomizes the semantic gateway labels and the purpose labels/initial states across seeds. An observation-free q using only prior actions and task times cannot select the correct manage/commit option or infer the negative-prefix purpose target for every occurrence, while the visible labels vary independently of I_t.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot exposes the fixed proxy labels, the one active drawer, each purpose statement, and its current answer buttons. A policy can read those static visible statements and choose the correct next button; no motion history is needed, so the configured 720 ms window (five frames) is more than sufficient and one endpoint frame would suffice.

clause_iii.reason: Waiting produces only timer/redraw activity. The simplified proxies remain fixed and available, purpose states do not change, and the one-drawer navigator is inert. The grader replays state changes only from submitted events and uses elapsed time only as a monotone value bounded by 180 seconds; a hard deadline or later completion is excluded by the definition. No grouped control mode has an action whose value strictly decreases due to non-clock autonomous task-state evolution within any positive delay.

common_visible_process: None. The only visible autonomous process is the timer/redraw loop, and with stationary gateways it supplies no changing task-state evidence and causes no expiring or degrading action opportunity; therefore it cannot witness clauses (i), (ii), and (iii) together.

pre_run.reason: The exact difficulty-2 construction removes motion, reset traps, and links, so all purpose-state work can be completed through the visible proxy buttons before the final administrative certification. The solver's prepare_solution performs the manage choice and all required purpose decisions before review and commit; its private-state reads are implementation evidence, while the same semantic choices are visible in the ledger. This uniform static construction supports the threshold judgment without asserting a numeric rate.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is the four-purpose, one-drawer, no-reset, no-link, stationary-gateway profile with orbit speed 0; simplified mode uses fixed proxies, and the observation bound is 720 ms with five frames.

A supplied control condition determines the generated parameters; gateway semantics and purpose labels/initial states are randomized per seed, which makes the visible state necessary for semantic choices but does not create autonomous motion.

Reset traps, directed links, drawers, and gateway surfaces are generated from the exact parameters; with reset_trap_count and link_count zero and drawer_count one, no coupling or reset process exists in this configuration.
Gateway selection is action-driven; currentPhase advances only when moving_gateways is true, while the animation-frame loop updates the timer and positions.
Simplified gateways render fixed decision proxies, the ledger renders explicit SET NO/SET YES controls, and stage/purpose/drawer changes occur only in input event handlers.
The simplified CSS disables direct orbit-card and physical switch interaction while presenting fixed proxy buttons; no CSS animation supplies a changing control target.

The grader binds the simplified input sources, replays only submitted events to mutate stage/drawer/purpose state, and checks terminal/final truth; elapsed task time is only required to be finite, monotone, and within 180 seconds.
The solver's visible-control workflow sets each purpose before review and then makes the final commit, providing structural evidence that required state-setting actions can be front-loaded.
The task verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent Consent Gauntlet grader.
